title: OpenACC offloading of the MFC compressible multiphase flow solver on AMD and NVIDIA GPUs
problem: Efficiently accelerating a compressible multiphase flow solver (MFC) across diverse GPU architectures. The challenge involves optimizing compute kernels and data movement for both NVIDIA and AMD GPUs while maintaining performance portability.
motivation: GPUs are central to modern supercomputers, and efficient acceleration of scientific computing applications is critical for high-performance computing performance and capability.
method: It uses OpenACC compiler directives (instructions that tell the compiler to offload code to GPUs, with special parallelization clauses like gang, vector, and collapse) to move computation to GPUs, and reorganizes the data layout by packing user-defined types into coalesced arrays (memory structures organized for efficient GPU access). It also uses code generation (metaprogramming) to eliminate function-call overhead by replacing function calls with their actual code (inlining). These three optimization strategies combine to achieve cumulative speedups.
key_novelty: It combines three optimization techniques: OpenACC directives with gang/vector/collapse clauses, data packing into coalesced arrays (memory organized for efficient GPU access), and metaprogramming-based function inlining (code generation to eliminate call overhead), achieving 6-30x speedups on both NVIDIA and AMD GPUs.
contributions: Demonstrated efficient OpenACC-based acceleration of MFC solver on both NVIDIA (V100) and AMD Instinct (MI250X) GPUs
Showed gang/vector/collapse directive optimization achieves 6-10x speedups through parallelism specification
Achieved 7x speedup via array packing and 30x speedup on select kernels on Frontier through data structure and inlining optimizations
Demonstrated strong scaling efficiency of 92% on MI250X with 16x device scaling using GPU-aware MPI, and weak scaling efficiency of 95-97% to 50-87% of Frontier and Summit
limitations: Evaluation limited to specific GPU architectures and does not compare against alternative acceleration approaches or CPU baseline performance.
primary_theme: GPU acceleration via OpenACC directives and memory optimization for scientific computing
